name: CISplatin + Fluorouracil with concurrent radiation (definitive anal SCC, mitomycin-sparing)

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.histology: squamous cell carcinoma of the anus
biomarkers.note: A cisplatin-based fluoropyrimidine backbone concurrent with radiation is a recognised mitomycin-sparing alternative for definitive treatment of localized anal squamous cell carcinoma when mitomycin is contraindicated by marrow reserve or comorbidity. No routine molecular biomarker gate for regimen selection; DPYD testing advised before fluoropyrimidine exposure. General reference: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) / DeVita.

premedications.name: Cisplatin hydration
premedications.notes: Pre- and post-cisplatin IV hydration with attention to magnesium and potassium; use a highly emetogenic antiemetic regimen on cisplatin days.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: Cisplatin is highly emetogenic; give three-drug prophylaxis on cisplatin days.

supportiveCare: Single definitive concurrent chemoradiation course (NOT a repeating cycle): chemotherapy is delivered on days 1 to 4 and 29 to 32 within one radiation course; cycleLengthDays (42) encodes the approximately 6-week concurrent course and cycles is 1.
Fluoropyrimidine DPYD testing before starting (FDA boxed warning; ANAL footnote a).
Maintain renal function and electrolytes through cisplatin exposure; monitor for radiation dermatitis and proctitis.
monitoring: CBC before each chemotherapy administration and during nadir
renal function, magnesium, and potassium before each cisplatin dose
audiometry / neuropathy assessment for cumulative cisplatin toxicity if symptomatic
response assessment (clinical exam; imaging) after chemoradiation

doseModificationRules.condition: declining creatinine clearance or significant cytopenia
doseModificationRules.text: Reduce or hold the second chemotherapy administration (days 29 to 32) for renal impairment or myelosuppression; clinical review required.
Reduce dose or avoid fluorouracil in DPYD-deficient patients per FDA boxed warning; clinical review required.

drugs.name: CISplatin
drugs.notes: CISplatin 75 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 29, concurrent with radiation, as the mitomycin-sparing platinum backbone; a weekly-cisplatin schedule is an alternative at experienced centres. ISMP tall-man: CISplatin (distinguish from CARBOplatin). Requires vigorous hydration and electrolyte repletion. General reference: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) / DeVita.

drugs.name: Fluorouracil (continuous infusion)
drugs.notes: Fluorouracil 1000 mg/m2/day by continuous IV infusion on days 1 to 4 and 29 to 32, concurrent with radiation and paired with cisplatin. DPYD testing advised before starting (FDA boxed warning). General reference: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) / DeVita.
